articles.title: Australian Minister Julian Hill joins Sri Lankan Buddhist monks for Kathina ceremony
articles.text:
Australian Assistant Minister for Citizenship, Customs and Multicultural Affairs and International Education, Julian Hill, has participated in a traditional Buddhist Kathina ceremony with Sri Lankan Buddhist monks in Australia.
The Australian minister shared photographs of the occasion on his official Facebook page, showing him serving food to Buddhist monks as part of the religious observance.
“Kathina, a 2,500 year old Buddhist tradition,” Hill wrote in his Facebook post.
Kathina is an important annual Buddhist ceremony held following the conclusion of the three-month Vas retreat, during which devotees offer robes and other necessities to Buddhist monks.
Hill, who represents the Bruce electorate in the Australian Federal Parliament, has served as a federal parliamentarian since 2016.
articles.summary: Australian Assistant Minister for Citizenship, Customs and Multicultural Affairs and International Education, Julian Hill, has participated in a traditional Buddhist Kathina ceremony with Sri Lankan Buddhist monks in Australia. The Australian minister shared photographs of the occasion on his official Facebook page, showing him serving food to Buddhist monks as part of the religious observance.

articles.title: 36th National Youth Sports Festival begins in Diyagama
articles.text:
The 36th National Youth Sports Festival commenced on Oct. 30 at the Mahinda Rajapaksa Stadium in Diyagama. The three-day festival will continue until Nov. 1.
The opening ceremony was held under the patronage of Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development Bimal Rathnayake and Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports Sunil Kumara Gamage.
Deputy Minister of Youth Affairs Dinindu Saman Hennayake, National Youth Services Council Chairman and Director General Attorney-at-Law Supun Wijerathna, and National Federation of Youth Clubs Secretary Mithin Gihan Priyasad also attended the event.
Organised annually by the National Youth Services Council, the National Youth Sports Festival provides a platform to identify sporting talent among Youth Club members across Grama Niladhari divisions and create opportunities for them to progress to the national level.
Member of Parliament Aruna Panagoda, National Youth Services Council officials, youth leaders of the National Federation of Youth Clubs and other invited guests were also present at the opening ceremony.

He also highlighted the importance of creating opportunities for young people through music, entertainment and cultural activities.

articles.title: Sri Lanka’s IT/BPO export earnings drop 15.5% in 2026
articles.text:
Sri Lanka’s earnings from computer and IT/BPO services declined by 15.5% during the first nine months of 2026, according to the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL).
The latest External Sector Performance report showed that earnings from computer and IT/BPO services fell to US$ 524.9 million during January–September 2026, compared to US$ 621 million during the corresponding period last year.
In September alone, earnings from the sector declined by 7.2% to US$ 65 million, compared to US$ 70 million in September 2025.
The decline comes despite an overall increase in Sri Lanka’s services export earnings during September.
According to the Central Bank, total services inflows increased by 11.2% to US$ 559.5 million during the month, compared to US$ 503.1 million a year earlier.
However, cumulative services inflows declined marginally by 0.6% to US$ 5.26 billion during January–September.
Meanwhile, earnings from sea and air transport services increased by 46.3% to US$ 199 million in September.
The Central Bank reported that Sri Lanka’s overall services account surplus declined by 22.3% to US$ 2.21 billion during the first nine months of 2026.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka’s earnings from computer and IT/BPO services declined by 15.5% during the first nine months of 2026, according to the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL). The latest External Sector Performance report showed that earnings from computer and IT/BPO services fell to US$ 524.9 million during January–September 2026, compared to US$ 621 million during the corresponding period last year.

articles.title: More tax cuts coming in 2027 Budget, President AKD announces
articles.text:
President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has announced that the government plans to reduce certain taxes further in the upcoming Budget while ensuring that state revenue targets are not affected.
Speaking about the country’s economic performance, the President said the government had achieved its revenue targets without introducing any new taxes since taking office.
“We have not imposed any new taxes since coming to power. In fact, we have significantly reduced some existing taxes. We will reduce certain taxes further in the upcoming Budget,” the President said.
He stressed that the proposed reductions would be implemented without jeopardising the government’s revenue targets.
The President said previous governments had repeatedly failed to meet their projected revenue targets, often collecting only around 90 percent of the expected amount.
However, he said the current administration had exceeded its revenue expectations, while maintaining a primary budget surplus that would help reduce the country’s debt burden over time.
He also acknowledged that rising inflation had placed additional pressure on households, particularly through higher prices for goods and services.
The President attributed much of the inflationary pressure to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and disruptions to international supply routes.
articles.summary: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has announced that the government plans to reduce certain taxes further in the upcoming Budget while ensuring that state revenue targets are not affected. We will reduce certain taxes further in the upcoming Budget,” the President said.

articles.title: IFC discusses support for Sri Lanka’s financial sector and economic development
articles.text:
A delegation from the International Finance Corporation (IFC), led by Regional Vice President Sarvesh Suri, held discussions with Labour Minister and Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning Dr. Anil Jayantha Fernando on ways to support Sri Lanka’s financial sector and promote sustainable economic growth.
The meeting was held on Oct. 30 at the Ministry of Finance, where both parties explored opportunities for IFC assistance in strengthening the country’s financial system and advancing inclusive economic development.
Discussions also focused on the possibility of securing IFC investment and financial assistance for Sri Lanka’s strategic development projects, particularly in agriculture, fisheries, tourism, transport and logistics.
The need to establish financing mechanisms beyond conventional banking practices, while aligning them with the country’s broader development priorities, was also highlighted.
The participants emphasized the importance of strengthening cooperation with the IFC to expand investment opportunities, improve the financial sector and support sustainable economic growth.
IFC Regional Director Manuel Reyes Retana and World Bank Group Country Manager for Sri Lanka and the Maldives David Sislen also attended the meeting, along with other representatives.

articles.title: UAE cuts petrol and diesel prices for November after three months of increases
articles.text:
The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has announced reductions in petrol and diesel prices for November 2026, offering relief to motorists following three consecutive months of price increases.
According to the revised fuel prices, Super 98 petrol will cost AED 4.16 (approximately Rs. 376) per litre in November, down from AED 4.40 in October, representing a reduction of AED 0.24.
Special 95 petrol will also fall by AED 0.24, from AED 4.28 to AED 4.04 (approximately Rs. 366) per litre.
Meanwhile, E-Plus 91 petrol will be priced at AED 3.97 (approximately Rs. 359) per litre, compared with AED 4.21 in October, marking a similar reduction of AED 0.24.
Diesel prices have also been reduced, although by a smaller margin, from AED 4.80 to AED 4.75 (approximately Rs. 430) per litre.
The revised prices will take effect on November 1 across the UAE.
The reductions amount to approximately 5.5% to 5.7% for petrol, while diesel prices will fall by about 1%.
The price cuts follow three consecutive months of increases, amid volatility in international energy markets linked to the Middle East conflict.
The UAE reviews and adjusts domestic fuel prices monthly to reflect developments in international energy markets.
articles.summary: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has announced reductions in petrol and diesel prices for November 2026, offering relief to motorists following three consecutive months of price increases. According to the revised fuel prices, Super 98 petrol will cost AED 4.16 (approximately Rs. 376) per litre in November, down from AED 4.40 in October, representing a reduction of AED 0.24.

articles.title: Bitumen shortage delays road construction projects in Sri Lanka: Central Bank
articles.text:
A shortage of bitumen caused by disruptions to imports from the Middle East continues to delay several road construction projects in Sri Lanka, despite overall growth in the country’s construction sector, according to the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL).
In its latest Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) report for September 2026, the Central Bank identified the shortage of bitumen, a key material used in road construction, as a major constraint affecting ongoing projects.
The report revealed that Sri Lanka’s construction sector continued to expand in September, recording a PMI of 57.8, compared to 59.4 in August.
Although the index remained above the 50-point threshold indicating expansion, the decline reflected a slower pace of growth.
The shortage of bitumen has been linked to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which have affected supplies from Iran, a major source of bitumen for Sri Lanka.
According to the Road Development Authority (RDA), imports from Iran have been disrupted since February/March 2026, creating difficulties for road maintenance and development projects.
RDA Director General N. A. Hettiarachchi previously stated that Sri Lanka requires at least 20,000 metric tonnes of bitumen every month for road maintenance and development activities.
The RDA has begun sourcing limited quantities from alternative markets, including Kazakhstan, Bahrain, China, India, Malaysia and Thailand. However, shipping difficulties and insurance restrictions linked to the Middle East conflict have complicated efforts to secure adequate supplies.
Meanwhile, the Central Bank said overall construction activity was supported by a sustained flow of new projects, particularly government-funded developments.
The New Orders Index increased from 62.5 in August to 65.6 in September, reflecting stronger demand for construction work.
However, the sector continued to face challenges, including shortages of construction materials and skilled workers.
The Employment Index stood at 58.1 in September, indicating continued recruitment, although many construction companies reported difficulties in finding skilled labour.
Suppliers’ delivery times also lengthened further, reflecting continued supply-side pressures.
Despite these challenges, construction companies remained optimistic about activity over the next three months, supported by newly awarded projects.
The Central Bank noted that material availability and skilled labour shortages remained ongoing challenges for the sector.
articles.summary: A shortage of bitumen caused by disruptions to imports from the Middle East continues to delay several road construction projects in Sri Lanka, despite overall growth in the country’s construction sector, according to the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL).

articles.text:
A man has been fined Rs. 310,000 by the Kahata­gasdigiliya Magistrate’s Court for setting up a trap gun allegedly intended to injure or kill a wild elephant and possessing the firearm without a licence, according to the Department of Wildlife Conservation.
The suspect was arrested on October 24 by a team of wildlife officers led by M.A.K.S. Dissanayake, Wildlife Site Assistant at the Kahata­gasdigiliya Wildlife Beat Office, during a patrol along the boundary of the Kokebe Forest Reserve in the Kahata­gasdigiliya Divisional Secretariat Division.
Officers discovered the trap gun set up on the boundary of private land, the department said.
The suspect and the seized firearm were produced before the Kahata­gasdigiliya Magistrate’s Court on October 25. Charges were filed on October 30, following which the magistrate imposed a fine of Rs. 310,000.
The Department of Wildlife Conservation said patrols would continue in the Kahata­gasdigiliya wildlife beat area to detect and prevent wildlife-related offences.

articles.title: Thai lawyer who questioned monarchy dressed as Harry Potter jailed for over 34 years
articles.text:
A Thai human rights lawyer who publicly questioned the country’s monarchy while dressed as Harry Potter during a protest has received cumulative prison sentences exceeding 34 years under Thailand’s strict royal defamation law.
Arnon Nampa, 42, was sentenced to another two years and eight months in prison by a Bangkok court on Friday (30), bringing his total prison term to more than 34 years, according to the BBC and AFP.
Arnon rose to prominence during Thailand’s student-led pro-democracy protests in 2020, when tens of thousands of demonstrators demanded political reforms and greater accountability from the country’s powerful monarchy.
In August 2020, he appeared at a Harry Potter-themed demonstration dressed as the fictional wizard and delivered a speech calling for greater public scrutiny of the monarchy, challenging a long-standing taboo in Thai society.
His latest conviction relates to a separate protest held outside the headquarters of Siam Commercial Bank in November 2020, where demonstrators questioned the management of royal assets and called for greater transparency.
Arnon and four other activists received prison sentences of two years and eight months each under Thailand’s lèse-majesté law, also known as Section 112 of the Criminal Code.
The legislation criminalises defaming, insulting or threatening the king, queen, heir-apparent or regent and carries severe prison sentences.
Arnon has been imprisoned since 2023 over multiple convictions linked to his protest activities and social media posts.
According to the BBC, he has faced 14 cases under the royal defamation law, with verdicts in two cases still pending.
His lawyer, Krisadang Nutcharut, criticised the use of the legislation against political activists, arguing that it had become a tool to silence opponents.
Thailand’s monarchy has traditionally occupied a highly protected position in the country’s political system, with criticism of the royal institution subject to criminal prosecution.
According to the BBC, 294 people have been prosecuted under the lèse-majesté law since 2020, with some receiving prison sentences of up to 50 years.
Arnon’s case has attracted international attention over concerns about freedom of expression and the treatment of pro-democracy activists in Thailand.
The cumulative sentence arises from multiple convictions rather than solely from his Harry Potter-themed protest speech.
articles.summary: A Thai human rights lawyer who publicly questioned the country’s monarchy while dressed as Harry Potter during a protest has received cumulative prison sentences exceeding 34 years under Thailand’s strict royal defamation law.

articles.title: Cardinal Malcolm Ranjith led delegation meets Presidential Secretary over environmental issues
articles.text:
A delegation led by Cardinal Malcolm Ranjith met Secretary to the President Dr. Nandika Sanath Kumanayake at the Presidential Secretariat on the 30th to discuss environmental issues affecting Muthurajawela, the Negombo Lagoon and several areas in the Gampaha District.
The discussion focused on environmental damage to the Muthurajawela wetlands, coastal degradation along the Pamunugama coastline and industrial-related issues in Liyanagemulla, Seeduwa.
Following the discussion, the Secretary to the President instructed relevant officials to take necessary measures to prevent further environmental damage in the affected areas.
It was also decided to establish committees comprising public representatives and community organisations to identify sustainable solutions to the issues.
The meeting was attended by Bishop J. D. Anthony, Rev. Fr. Cyril Gamini, Rev. Fr. Nilantha Heshan, Members of Parliament Lasith Bhashana Gamage and Stephanie Fernando, senior government officials, representatives of the Ministry of Environment, Catholic clergy and other invitees.

articles.title: US dollar rises by Rs. 22.62 against Sri Lankan rupee in first 9 months of 2026
articles.text:
The Sri Lankan rupee has depreciated by 6.8% against the US dollar during the first ten months of 2026, according to the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL).
In its latest External Sector Performance report, the Central Bank revealed that the exchange rate stood at Rs. 332.61 per US dollar at the end of October 2026, compared to Rs. 309.99 at the end of 2025.
This represents an increase of Rs. 22.62 in the rupee value of one US dollar during the ten-month period.
The Central Bank’s figures also show that the exchange rate stood at Rs. 292.58 per US dollar at the end of 2024, indicating a continued depreciation of the rupee against the dollar over the past two years.
The depreciation means that more Sri Lankan rupees are now required to purchase one US dollar, potentially increasing the local currency cost of imports and other dollar-denominated payments.
Meanwhile, Sri Lanka’s gross official reserves stood at US$ 6.9 billion at the end of September 2026, including the swap facility with the People’s Bank of China.
The Central Bank also reported that Sri Lanka’s merchandise trade deficit widened to US$ 7.9 billion during January–September 2026, compared to US$ 5.2 billion during the corresponding period last year.
However, the monthly trade deficit narrowed to US$ 731 million in September, supported by stronger merchandise export earnings.
The latest figures were released as part of the Central Bank’s External Sector Performance report for September 2026.
articles.summary: The Sri Lankan rupee has depreciated by 6.8% against the US dollar during the first ten months of 2026, according to the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL). In its latest External Sector Performance report, the Central Bank revealed that the exchange rate stood at Rs. 332.61 per US dollar at the end of October 2026, compared to Rs. 309.99 at the end of 2025.

articles.title: Canada has ‘learned we are overdependent on the US’ – PM Mark Carney
articles.text:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney spoke to DW on Friday after talks in Montreal with European Union leaders seeking to hammer out details of a new, closer partnership between Canada and the EU.
Amid difficult negotiations with US President Donald Trump, representing Canada’s biggest trading partner, Carney said that he and his compatriots had come to realize the country was too dependent on the economic powerhouse to the south.
“The lesson we’ve taken, Canadians as a whole, is we’re overdependent on the United States. Too closely connected to the United States. And we need to build our strength here at home and diversify and deepen our partnerships with like-minded countries internationally,” Carney said.
An EU delegation led by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa held talks with Carney and other Canadian officials in Montreal on Friday.
They’re discussing the plans floated by Commission President Ursula von der Leyen to forge what she called an “associate membership” — a status that does not yet exist for any other country — even as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s government resists creating this label. Carney seemed to speak in its favor.
“Well, I think the advantage of what we’re doing is that a few things are absolutely clear, irrespective of the exact terminology that’s used. President von der Leyen uses associated membership. We use associated membership,” he told DW’s Katharina Kroll at Port of Montreal Tower.
“What does that mean? It means the closest possible partnership without being a full member of the European Union, because Canada is not in Europe geographically and therefore cannot have accession.” Carney said.
What scope for EU-Canada cooperation does Carney see?
Asked if he was looking to create a “new transatlantic bloc without the US,” Carney said it was more about diversifying and deepening Canada’s other partnerships than excluding by far its largest trading partner.
“We’re both partners of the United States, obviously close partners, alliance partners in NATO. And there are many, many opportunities for cooperation with the United States,” he said. “But in many cases, there’ll be much deeper cooperation for Canada between Canada and Europe than Canada and the United States.”
He mentioned both existing areas of cooperation like the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), calling it “one of the most successful free trade agreements in the world,” and also pointed to research cooperation and programs like Horizon Europe and Erasmus+ enabling student exchanges.
But Carney also pointed to areas where the two sides could seek to expand cooperation, naming areas like space technologies, artificial intelligence and critical minerals.
Is Canada concerned the talks could alienate the US, or Trump?
Despite his well-documented difficulties with Donald Trump — perhaps most crudely exemplified by Trump’s attempts to unilaterally rename Lake Ontario, or his posting AI videos imagining him as an ice hockey player beating Carney up in a fight — Carney said US-Canadian ties were too deep to be derailed by any governments or prime ministers or presidents.
“The bonds between Canadians and Americans are longstanding. They’re very strong. And big elements of that will be maintained regardless of the government in Canada, the government in the United States, the combination of the two,” he said.
Asked about the best way to deal with Trump, Carney said it was “to be direct, to be clear, to be absolutely clear about your bottom lines are.” He said it was important to show respect but also to continue to bring “the negotiations back to the core issues.”
But he said the tensions with Trump had demonstrated the need to diversify and to seek Canada’s other most natural partners around the world.
He acknowledged that no matter the nature of the talks with the EU, “the scale of the relationship with the United States” would be “very hard to replace.”
Asked if he was concerned that the talks could expose him to further tariffs or other punitive measures from the Trump administration, Carney said, “We’ve been living with this for some time.”
“There have been many justifications for trade action against Canada that the United States has had,” he said. “Our view is that all of them are unjustified under our trade agreement.”
Carney said the crucial message, also for the Trump White House, was that the talks with Brussels concerned a “positive association” and partnership “to help solve global problems” and address global challenges.
“It’s not against somebody. It’s for. It’s a positive act,” he said. (DW)

articles.title: Sri Lanka’s fuel import bill jumps 51.5% to US$ 4.5 billion
articles.text:
Sri Lanka’s expenditure on fuel imports increased by 51.5% during the first nine months of 2026 compared to the corresponding period last year, according to the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL).
The latest External Sector Performance report revealed that cumulative fuel import expenditure reached approximately US$ 4.5 billion during January–September 2026.
However, the Central Bank noted that monthly expenditure on fuel imports declined for the fifth consecutive month in September.
Despite this recent downward trend in monthly spending, the overall fuel import bill remained significantly higher than during the same period last year.
Meanwhile, Sri Lanka’s total merchandise import expenditure increased by 21.3% to US$ 18.67 billion during the first nine months of 2026, compared to US$ 15.39 billion during the corresponding period in 2025.
In September alone, total merchandise imports increased by 2.9% to US$ 2.11 billion.
The higher cumulative import expenditure contributed to a widening of Sri Lanka’s merchandise trade deficit, which reached US$ 7.91 billion during January–September 2026, compared to US$ 5.17 billion in the corresponding period last year.

The cumulative services account surplus also declined by 22.3% to US$ 2.21 billion during the first nine months of 2026.
The Central Bank attributed the reduction in the services surplus mainly to increased payments for travel and air transport services, which outpaced growth in services inflows.

articles.title: TIN Certificate mandatory for key transactions from tomorrow
articles.text:
A valid Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) Certificate will become mandatory from tomorrow (November 1) for several key transactions, including opening bank accounts, registering vehicles and land, registering businesses and obtaining credit cards, the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) said.
The requirement is being introduced under the Inland Revenue (Amendment) Act, No. 11 of 2026, and applies to transactions specified under Section 102(3) of the Inland Revenue Act.
Accordingly, individuals will be required to submit a valid TIN Certificate when opening accounts at banks or financial institutions, obtaining building plan approvals, registering motor vehicles, renewing vehicle licences, registering land or land titles, registering businesses, transferring shares in Sri Lankan companies and obtaining credit cards.
For company share transfers, both the buyer and seller must provide their TIN details.
The IRD has instructed relevant officials and institutions to verify that the required TIN documentation is submitted before processing or completing these transactions.
The Department has advised individuals who have not yet obtained a TIN to apply in advance through its e-Services platform.
Individuals can also verify their TIN through the IRD’s e-Services portal. A printout of the verification result displaying the individual’s National Identity Card (NIC) number and TIN will be accepted as an alternative to the official certificate.
The IRD reiterated that obtaining a TIN is mandatory for all resident individuals who were 18 or older by December 31, 2023, as well as those who turned 18 on or after January 1, 2024, upon reaching that age. (Newswire/AI Image)

articles.title: October 17 power outage: Norochcholai unit failure triggered outage, preliminary report says
articles.text:
The sudden disconnection of 187 megawatts of electricity from the first unit of the Norochcholai Lakvijaya Power Plant triggered the islandwide power system collapse on October 17, according to a preliminary investigation report submitted by the National System Operator (NSO) to the Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka (PUCSL).
The report states that the generating unit disconnected at around 11.43 a.m. within 450 milliseconds, causing the system frequency to drop to 48.75 hertz. The entire national power system collapsed within 4.1 seconds, as a result, the report said.
All five stages of the Under Frequency Load Shedding (UFLS) mechanism were activated in an attempt to stabilise the system. However, the protection measures failed to prevent the collapse, resulting in the disconnection of 449.2 megawatts, or 39.6% of the 1,135 megawatts being generated immediately before the outage.
Generating units at several hydropower stations, including Victoria, Kotmale, Randenigala, Samanalawewa and Laxapana, were also shut down following the activation of their protection systems.
The NSO began restoration operations immediately after the incident. Electricity supplies were restored through four systems — Mahaweli, Laxapana, Samanalawewa/Southern and Colombo — using several hydropower plants and the Kelanitissa Power Plant.
All main substations were restored by 4.58 p.m., while the complete restoration of the national transmission system took five hours and 15 minutes, the report said.
The restoration process also encountered technical issues and operational delays at certain generating units. A technical problem in an auxiliary system delayed the restarting of a generating unit at the Yugadanavi Power Plant.
However, the preliminary investigation has not identified the root cause of the sudden disconnection of the Norochcholai unit.
The NSO said a detailed investigation report would be submitted to the PUCSL at a later date.
articles.summary: The sudden disconnection of 187 megawatts of electricity from the first unit of the Norochcholai Lakvijaya Power Plant triggered the islandwide power system collapse on October 17, according to a preliminary investigation report submitted by the National System Operator (NSO) to the Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka (PUCSL).

articles.title: Oil jumps 2%, settles at 6-month highs on fears of escalation in Iran
articles.text:
Oil prices jumped more than 2% on Friday and settled ​at their highest levels since the end of April, as traders braced for a potential escalation in the Iran war after the US midterm elections, ‌with an attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz highlighting supply risks.
Brent crude futures for December , which expired on Friday, settled up $2.76, or 2.4%, at $117.64 a barrel, after touching a high of $118. The more active January contract gained $2.63 to $113.43.
US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures settled $2.12, or 2.08%, higher at $104.12.
For the month, Brent finished 13.6% higher, while WTI rose 15.2%. “Traders will remain ​focused on oil flows out of the Middle East and the likely escalation by US and allied forces,” said Dennis Kissler, senior vice president ​of trading at BOK Financial.
On Friday, a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was hit by explosive devices attached by a small ⁠boat, said the UKMTO, the British maritime security service. It was not immediately clear who was behind the attack in the strait, the key sea outlet for ​Gulf crude and fuel supplies.
It was the first known successful strike in the waterway using limpet mines, explosives that are attached to a ship’s hull from a small boat, ​since the US-Israeli war with Iran began in February, maritime sources said.
‘HIGHER LIKELIHOOD OF AN ESCALATION’
The US ordered non-emergency government employees and their family members to leave Saudi Arabia effective October 23 due to safety risks, the US embassy in Riyadh said on Friday, citing Houthi attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure.
Yemen’s Iranian-backed Houthi militants said on Thursday they had attacked ​several sites in Saudi Arabia, including the large Ras Tanura oil refinery, the Rabigh refinery and a production facility in Abqaiq owned by state oil company Saudi ​Aramco.
A Saudi-led coalition also said it had intercepted a cruise missile launched by the Houthis towards the kingdom’s western region.
Meanwhile, Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on Friday as part of coordinated efforts to ‌reach a ⁠deal between the US and Iran, an official briefed on the talks told Reuters.
US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that Vice President JD Vance had reached out to Iran to help the country get medical supplies, after US media reported Vance had written to Tehran’s top security official to revive peace talks.
Iran has received a letter from Vance, but it has not responded to it yet, Iran’s semi-official Tasnim news agency reported, adding that Tehran wants the US to meet its conditions and “any ​position that contradicts this framework is ​unacceptable.”
Oil prices could become even more ⁠volatile in the next couple of weeks due to Israel’s recent elections and the US midterm elections on November 3, according to a Saxo Bank briefing on Thursday.
The Danish bank said crude is expected to trade in a higher range of $70 ​to $90 a barrel even after the conflict ends, compared with a pre-war range of $60 to $70.
articles.summary: Oil prices jumped more than 2% on Friday and settled ​at their highest levels since the end of April, as traders braced for a potential escalation in the Iran war after the US midterm elections, ‌with an attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz highlighting supply risks.

articles.text:
The Peterite Cricket League (PCL) is set to return after a 13-year break, with an eight-team franchise cricket tournament scheduled for November 7 and 8 at the St. Peter’s College grounds in Colombo.

The competition will feature eight franchises: Thambapanni Lions, Resistance Panthers, Bamba Patriots, Colombo Sports Hub, Top Knock Titans, Colombo Tuskers, Foundation Guardians and UK Peterites.
Matches will be played in a six-over format, with eight players per team.
Each franchise will include players from four age categories: current schoolboys, those aged 20–30, players aged 30–40 and those over 40.

The winning team will receive the Rev. Sunil Herman Perera Memorial Champions Trophy, while the runners-up will be awarded the Mr. Austin Fernando Memorial Shield.
The tournament is being organised under the leadership of Peterite Cricket Foundation President Hans Fernando and PCL Committee Chairman Lakshan Rodrigo.
The British School of Commerce, Colombo, has come forward as the main sponsor, with Dubai-based Steadfast Cargo Services LLC serving as the silver sponsor.
Rochelle Vanderwall, Head of Operations at the British School of Commerce, Colombo, said the institution was offering scholarship opportunities for deserving students who have demonstrated academic excellence and achievements in extracurricular activities.
She said the institution had also introduced new academic programmes, including a BBM degree and Qualifications Scotland Foundation and HND programmes leading to a degree from the University of Suffolk in the United Kingdom.
The tournament will also be supported by ThePapare as its official broadcasting partner, Hemas Hospitals as its medical partner, Ada Derana Sports as its media partner and CricWire as its online news partner, alongside several other partners.
Organisers said the return of the league forms part of a broader initiative to strengthen cricket at St. Peter’s College, nurture emerging talent and maintain connections between generations of Peterite cricketers.

articles.title: “UNP-SJB alliance not enough”: Ranil targets 8 million Gen Z, Millennial voters
articles.text:
Former President and United National Party (UNP) Leader Ranil Wickremesinghe says an alliance between the UNP and Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) alone will not guarantee an election victory, stressing the need to attract approximately eight million Gen Z and Millennial voters ahead of the next election.
Wickremesinghe said many younger voters have not yet decided which political party to support and that winning their confidence would be crucial for future electoral success.
“Some believe that if the UNP and SJB unite, we will win. That is not the case,” he said.
The former President said Sri Lanka’s political landscape has changed significantly and that traditional political strategies would no longer be sufficient to secure election victories.
He stressed that the UNP, which has a history spanning 65 years, must develop a new political identity to appeal to younger generations.
Wickremesinghe said Gen Z and Millennial voters represent a significant section of the electorate, with approximately eight million people belonging to these groups, according to his estimate.
He noted that many younger voters had become disillusioned with traditional politics, particularly following Sri Lanka’s economic collapse in 2022.
Referring to youth-led political movements in Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Nepal and Serbia, Wickremesinghe said younger generations were increasingly influencing political developments across the world.
He said the UNP had already begun working with two groups, Millennium UNP and Gen Z UNP, as part of efforts to transform the party and attract younger supporters.
According to Wickremesinghe, these groups are exploring new methods of political organisation, moving away from the traditional system of establishing party branches and instead focusing initially on connecting with people through digital platforms.
He said political parties could no longer depend solely on their traditional voter bases or alliances to secure electoral victories.
Wickremesinghe warned that without attracting younger voters, political parties would struggle to move forward, regardless of whether they formed alliances.
He called for a new approach to rebuilding the UNP’s political identity, placing Gen Z and Millennial voters at the centre of its future strategy.

The Department of the Registrar of Companies has issued a final warning to companies that have failed to submit their Beneficial Ownership information, cautioning that continued non-compliance could result in legal action, including fines of up to Rs. 1 million or imprisonment for up to 10 years.

According to the notice, failure to comply with the statutory requirements relating to Beneficial Ownership constitutes an offence under the Companies Act, No. 7 of 2007, as amended by the Companies (Amendment) Act, No. 12 of 2025.
The department warned that continued non-compliance could result in legal action and penalties prescribed by law, including, where applicable, a fine not exceeding Rs. 1 million, imprisonment for a period not exceeding 10 years, or both.
Beneficial Ownership information identifies the individuals who ultimately own or control a company, helping improve corporate transparency and accountability.
The Registrar General urged all affected companies to immediately submit and regularise outstanding information through the department’s Beneficial Ownership System.
The notice stressed that companies must ensure immediate compliance with the legal requirements.

articles.title: SC orders 3 police officers to compensate businessman tortured and forced to hand over gold
articles.text:
The Supreme Court has ruled that three police officers attached to the Negombo Divisional Criminal Investigation Department violated the fundamental rights of a jewellery businessman from Kuliyapitiya by subjecting him to physical assault, harassment and unlawful detention during a police investigation.
The court ordered the three officers to personally pay Rs. 100,000 each, amounting to Rs. 300,000, as compensation to the businessman.
The ruling was delivered by a three-judge bench comprising Justices A.L. Shiran Gooneratne, Mahinda Samayawardhena and Menaka Wijesundera.
The fundamental rights petition was filed by Sahul Hameed Sashek, also known as Shaul Hameed Mohamed Sufaik, a jewellery shop owner in Kuliyapitiya.
According to the judgment, the businessman alleged that police officers had assaulted and threatened him while investigating a case involving gold he had unknowingly purchased from a suspect.
He claimed that officers arrived at his home while he was away and threatened to arrest his wife and children unless he returned immediately.
Upon returning home, he alleged that he was handcuffed, forced to kneel and brutally assaulted in front of his wife and children.
The businessman further claimed that he was repeatedly assaulted inside a vehicle and forced to surrender gold and money to the officers.
According to the petition, CCTV cameras installed at his jewellery shop captured part of the incident involving the handing over of gold.
He also alleged that officers forced him to consume alcohol and threatened him against reporting the assaults to medical officers or the court.
The police officers denied the allegations, maintaining that the businessman had been lawfully arrested as part of an investigation and that gold items and foreign currency had been recovered.
However, the Supreme Court rejected their explanations, finding that the evidence presented by the petitioner supported his allegations.
Justice Menaka Wijesundera, delivering the judgment, observed that the officers’ denials were insufficiently credible to dismiss the businessman’s complaint.
The court also considered medical records and documentary evidence submitted by the petitioner.
Accordingly, the Supreme Court determined that Inspector D.R.A. Gihan Manohara and Police Constables M.A. Amal Sanjeewa and V.G. Bandara had violated the petitioner’s fundamental rights under Articles 11, 12(1) and 13(2) of the Constitution.
These provisions protect individuals against torture and cruel treatment, guarantee equality before the law and safeguard the rights of individuals held in custody.
The court ordered each of the three officers to pay Rs. 100,000 to the petitioner within six months.
Justices A.L. Shiran Gooneratne and Mahinda Samayawardhena agreed with the judgment delivered by Justice Menaka Wijesundera.
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled that three police officers attached to the Negombo Divisional Criminal Investigation Department violated the fundamental rights of a jewellery businessman from Kuliyapitiya by subjecting him to physical assault, harassment and unlawful detention during a police investigation.

The tourism earnings estimates are based on a revised methodology introduced by the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority (SLTDA) in May 2026, which incorporates country-specific visitor arrivals, average daily spending and average length of stay.

articles.title: Six arrested over assault on bus driver, conductor in Kalutara released on bail
articles.text:
Six suspects have been arrested in connection with the assault on a bus driver and conductor after a group of individuals travelling on two motorcycles intercepted their bus in Kalutara, police said.
The incident, which was captured on video and widely circulated on social media, reportedly occurred at around 9.00 p.m. on October 26 in the Nagas Junction area within the Kalutara North Police Division.
Kalutara North Police arrested all six suspects along with the two motorcycles allegedly used in the attack.
The suspects were produced before the Kalutara Magistrate’s Court on October 29, where they submitted sworn affidavits admitting responsibility for the offence.
The court sternly warned the suspects and ordered their release on personal bail of Rs. 500,000 each. The next date for the case was also announced.
Preliminary investigations have revealed that the assault stemmed from an earlier incident in Moratuwa, where the bus had stopped at a traffic signal and a person attempting to board was asked to get off by the conductor.

articles.title: Sri Lanka records highest-ever monthly merchandise exports in September
articles.text:
Sri Lanka recorded its highest-ever monthly merchandise export earnings in September 2026, reaching US$ 1.37 billion, according to the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL).
In its latest External Sector Performance report, the Central Bank said merchandise exports increased by 21% compared to September 2025, surpassing the previous record of US$ 1.30 billion recorded in July 2025.
Total merchandise export earnings during the first nine months of 2026 reached US$ 10.75 billion, reflecting a 5.3% increase compared to the corresponding period last year.
Meanwhile, services exports increased by 11.2% to US$ 559 million in September, although cumulative services export earnings declined by 0.6% to US$ 5.26 billion during January–September.
Combined exports of goods and services reached US$ 1.94 billion in September, an increase of 18% compared to the same month last year.
However, despite the record export performance, Sri Lanka’s merchandise trade deficit widened to US$ 7.9 billion during the first nine months of 2026, compared to US$ 5.2 billion during the corresponding period in 2025.
The Central Bank attributed the widening cumulative trade deficit to a faster increase in import expenditure, which rose by 21.3% to US$ 18.67 billion during January–September.
Nevertheless, the monthly trade deficit narrowed to US$ 731 million in September, compared to US$ 910 million a year earlier.

articles.title: “I never play the race card for the sake of it”: Sangakkara rejects Ryanair claims, reveals what happened at Dublin Airport
articles.text:
Sri Lankan cricket legend Kumar Sangakkara has rejected Ryanair’s claims that he refused to provide visa documents at Dublin Airport, revealing details of an alleged discriminatory encounter involving him and his wife.
In an interview with the Daily Mail, Sangakkara said a female staff member behaved rudely towards his family and made what he described as a racist remark while they were preparing to board a flight from Dublin to Bristol on Wednesday (28).
According to Sangakkara, the staff member told him: “You people with your kinds of passports should expect this.”
The former Sri Lankan captain said the incident occurred after confusion over the electronic visas required for his family, who were travelling on Sri Lankan passports.
Sangakkara explained that he had visited Ryanair’s visa check desk nearly two hours before boarding to ensure his family had completed the necessary procedures. He said staff had assured him that he would not need to display the electronic visas again at the boarding gate.
However, when the family reached the gate, they were asked to access and display the documents on their phones.
Sangakkara said he agreed to comply but requested additional time because accessing the electronic visas involved several steps.
He alleged that a female staff member repeatedly shouted at him to hurry up and threatened to close boarding.
When Sangakkara told her she was being rude, he said she accused him of being argumentative and aggressive and threatened to deny him boarding, claiming he could be considered a threat to other passengers.
His wife, Yehali, then intervened and challenged the staff member over her remarks.
Sangakkara said he considered the reference to their passports offensive and discriminatory.
Rejecting Ryanair’s earlier statement, Sangakkara said the airline’s claim that he had refused to provide his visa documents was completely untrue.
“I never play the race card for the sake of it, and this was an offensive comment,” he told the Daily Mail.
Ryanair had earlier maintained that Sangakkara refused to provide the required visa documentation when requested by a gate agent conducting mandatory immigration checks.
The airline said the family was eventually allowed to travel after the necessary checks were completed.
Sangakkara confirmed that he and his family boarded the flight but said the incident had left them deeply disappointed following an otherwise enjoyable visit to Dublin to celebrate his 49th birthday.
He has since submitted a formal complaint of approximately 2,000 words to Ryanair, detailing the incident, and said he was informed that a response could be expected within eight days.
Sangakkara said he had not sought publicity over the incident but believed such treatment should not happen to anyone.
“It’s just a case of this is wrong, and it shouldn’t have happened – to me or to anyone,” he said.
Ryanair’s publicly reported response addressed the visa-documentation issue but did not specifically respond to Sangakkara’s allegations of racism and discriminatory behaviour.(Newswire / Source: Daily Mail)
articles.summary: Sri Lankan cricket legend Kumar Sangakkara has rejected Ryanair’s claims that he refused to provide visa documents at Dublin Airport, revealing details of an alleged discriminatory encounter involving him and his wife. “I never play the race card for the sake of it, and this was an offensive comment,” he told the Daily Mail.

articles.title: Sri Lanka ready for Pakistan challenge as Kusal Mendis eyes tri-series title
articles.text:
Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis says his team is well prepared and determined to deliver a strong performance against Pakistan in Saturday’s ODI tri-series final at the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore.
Speaking ahead of the final, Mendis acknowledged Pakistan’s recent performances but expressed confidence in Sri Lanka’s preparations.
“The final is a big game for us. Pakistan have played good cricket in their recent matches. We are well prepared and looking forward to the final,” Mendis said.
Sri Lanka will enter the title clash with confidence after recording a convincing eight-wicket victory over Pakistan in their previous encounter on Tuesday.
In that match, left-arm pacer Dilshan Madushanka produced an outstanding bowling performance, taking five wickets for just 34 runs as Pakistan were dismissed for 110.
Sri Lanka comfortably chased down the target in 18.1 overs, with Kamindu Mendis scoring an unbeaten 62 to secure their place in the final.
“We played really well against Pakistan in our previous encounter. We have done several things right and are focused on following our processes and sticking to our basic plans,” the Sri Lankan captain said.
Sri Lanka also produced one of the highlights of the tournament with a remarkable eight-wicket victory over England in Rawalpindi, successfully chasing a target of 430 runs, the second-highest successful run chase in men’s ODI history.
Pavan Rathnayake has been among Sri Lanka’s standout performers during the tournament, while the team’s batting depth and recent bowling performances have provided encouragement ahead of the final.
Pakistan, meanwhile, were the first team to qualify for the final after registering three consecutive victories, including two wins over England and one against Sri Lanka.
However, their eight-wicket defeat to Sri Lanka in the final league encounter has added further interest to Saturday’s title clash.
Pakistan captain Shaheen Shah Afridi said his side would need to improve in certain areas, particularly top-order batting and building partnerships.
Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson also admitted that his team had yet to produce its best cricket in the tournament and expressed hope that it would come in the final.
Mendis, meanwhile, expressed appreciation for the support Sri Lanka have received both at home and in Pakistan.
“Everyone in Sri Lanka is very happy with our performances. Pakistan fans have also shown great support for Sri Lankan players, which is encouraging for us,” he said.
The final will begin at 1.30 p.m. Sri Lanka time on Saturday, with the toss scheduled for 1.00 p.m.
Sri Lanka will be looking to finish their tour with a trophy, while Pakistan will be aiming to secure their first ODI tri-series title on home soil.

articles.title: ‘They are trying to kill him’: Imran Khan’s son issues urgent warning over father’s life
articles.text:
Imran Khan’s son has said no one has heard from his father since August, when the former Pakistani prime minister claimed he was being tortured.
Sulaiman Khan, his son from his first marriage to British heiress Jemima Goldsmith, alleged that his father’s life was in danger and blamed Pakistan’s army chief General Asim Munir for his continued incarceration.
Mr Khan, 74, is serving a prison sentence at Rawalpindi’s notorious Adiala Jail following convictions on corruption and bribery charges. His family has repeatedly raised concerns about his treatment in prison and deteriorating health.
The former prime minister and Pakistan’s former national cricket captain, who faces charges in more than 100 cases, has been held in solitary confinement. He has denied all charges against him, describing them as politically motivated.
Sulaiman Khan said the family and his father’s lawyers had not heard from him in months.
He said his father had previously warned that he could suffer a similar fate to former Egyptian president Mohamed Morsi , who died during a court hearing in 2019.
“No one has seen or heard from my father since August, when he explicitly said that he was being tortured and that the regime was trying to kill him like Egypt ’s government did Morsi,” Sulaiman Khan wrote.
He accused General Munir of continuing to ignore an August Supreme Court order directing that Mr Khan be assessed and treated at the private Shifa International Hospital and granted regular visits from his family and access to his lawyers.
“It is clear that they are trying to kill him as he is by far the most popular political figure in the country, and they fear him. If the worst happens, no one should make any mistake who is responsible,” he added.
The government of Pakistan has denied allegations of mistreatment and solitary confinement.
Mr Khan isn’t being held under a government order but as a “convicted prisoner” serving sentences imposed by courts following judicial proceedings, the Ministry of Information told the Associated Press in a written response in August.
The allegations come as Sulaiman Khan and his brother Kasim Khan have reportedly been advised against travelling to Pakistan to campaign for their father’s release following the arrests of other family members.
Mr Khan’s three sisters, Aleema Khan, Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, were detained in September 2026 under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance ahead of planned protests.
Their detention was extended for another 30 days on Monday, according to officials from Pakistan’s Punjab government.
Mr Khan remains hugely popular in Pakistan despite his imprisonment. A rally demanding his release earlier this month drew thousands of supporters.
Protesters organised a long march towards Islamabad, demanding his release, improved access to him in prison and medical treatment by doctors of his choice.
On 11 October, president Asif Ali Zardari declared a state of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and suspended the provincial government led by Mr Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party.
The government cited Islamist militancy in the province bordering Afghanistan as the reason for the emergency. However, the PTI described the move as “more of a coup disguised as an emergency”, accusing the authorities of attempting to weaken the movement demanding Mr Khan’s release. (The Independent)

articles.title: SC rejects People’s Leasing’s US$700,000 insurance claim against Amana Takaful
articles.text:
The Supreme Court has dismissed an appeal filed by People’s Leasing and Finance PLC against Amana Takaful PLC over a US$700,000 insurance claim relating to a vessel that sank in 2009.
A three-judge bench comprising Justices Mahinda Samayawardhena, Dr Sobhitha Rajakaruna and Sampath K.B. Wijeratne upheld the Commercial High Court’s earlier decision to reject the claim.
The dispute arose after the Maldivian-flagged vessel M.V. Medhufaru sank on May 31, 2009.
People’s Leasing, which retained legal ownership of the vessel under a lease agreement with Sawahil Lines (Pvt) Ltd, had obtained a Hull Takaful insurance policy from Amana Takaful.
Following the sinking, People’s Leasing sought US$700,000 in compensation, arguing that the vessel had encountered severe monsoon weather while travelling from India to the Maldives.
However, Amana Takaful rejected the claim, maintaining that the vessel was unseaworthy and that the required classification certification had not been maintained.
The Supreme Court found that the vessel, which was approximately 33 years old, had suffered from corrosion, holes in its hull and continuous water leakage before sinking.
The Court observed that adverse weather alone could not establish the insurer’s liability when evidence indicated that the vessel’s physical condition had materially contributed to the sinking.
A key issue was the vessel’s classification under the Indian Register of Shipping (IRS).
The Court found that the vessel’s IRS classification certificate had expired in September 2008, several months before the sinking, and had not been renewed.
The judges ruled that maintaining the agreed classification was an express condition of the insurance policy and that its breach provided an independent basis for rejecting the claim.
The Court also rejected People’s Leasing’s argument that the Islamic Takaful nature of the insurance arrangement prevented Amana Takaful from relying on the policy’s contractual conditions.
Justice Dr Sobhitha Rajakaruna, delivering the judgment, held that the principles governing Takaful insurance did not override the express contractual obligations agreed upon by the parties.
The judgment also examined a dispute over unpaid insurance premiums, noting that the outstanding balance had been settled after the vessel sank. However, the Court found it unnecessary to determine that issue separately because the breaches relating to seaworthiness and classification were sufficient to uphold the dismissal.
Accordingly, the Supreme Court dismissed the appeal and affirmed the Commercial High Court’s October 2018 judgment, without awarding costs in the Supreme Court proceedings.
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has dismissed an appeal filed by People’s Leasing and Finance PLC against Amana Takaful PLC over a US$700,000 insurance claim relating to a vessel that sank in 2009. The Court also rejected People’s Leasing’s argument that the Islamic Takaful nature of the insurance arrangement prevented Amana Takaful from relying on the policy’s contractual conditions.

articles.title: Sri Lanka Partners with World Bank and IFAD to launch $665 Mn AgriConnect plan
articles.text:
The Government of Sri Lanka, in partnership with the World Bank Group and the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), has officially launched the Sri Lanka AgriConnect Joint Implementation Plan to modernize the nation’s agrifood sector, create jobs, and strengthen food security.
“Sri Lanka is committed to transforming our agrifood sector from one that primarily produces commodities to one that creates greater value, better jobs and stronger opportunities for rural communities. Our farmers, fishers and rural communities are not simply beneficiaries of development, they are partners in building a stronger, more productive and more resilient economy. The AgriConnect Joint Implementation Plan will directly catalyze Government action under our Public Investment Programme, helping us connect farmers to finance, technology and markets while creating better jobs, attracting private investment and expanding opportunities across rural Sri Lanka,” said Dr. Harini Amarasuriya, Prime Minister of Sri Lanka.
Aligned with the Government’s national development agenda, the Public Investment Programme 2026-2030, and the World Bank Group’s Country Partnership Framework, the initiative aims to assist 900,000 farmers in accessing agricultural value chains by 2030. The plan is backed by $550 million in World Bank Group investments and $115 million from IFAD, alongside efforts to mobilize up to $170 million in private capital over the next five years.
Highlighting the sector’s potential, where agriculture and food processing account for at least 15% of Sri Lanka’s GDP, 30% of goods exports, and one in three jobs, Sarvesh Suri, IFC Regional Vice President for Asia and the Pacific, noted: “Sri Lanka has globally competitive agricultural products and strong entrepreneurial potential. The priority now is to connect farmers and agribusinesses with the finance, technology and markets they need to scale. By aligning public and private investment – from innovative financing to risk-sharing solutions – AgriConnect can unlock capital, strengthen agribusinesses and create more and better jobs.”
Sri Lanka is the first South Asian country to join AgriConnect, which will focus on key value chains including coconut, cinnamon, tea, fisheries, dairy, poultry, aquaculture, and horticulture, with a special emphasis on expanding opportunities in lagging regions like the Northern and Eastern Provinces.
Regarding the implementation on the ground, Donal Brown, IFAD Associate Vice-President, Department for Country Operations stated, “There is a real opportunity to build on the progress already made in Sri Lanka’s rural economy and ensure that investments continue to reach smallholder farmers. Through AgriConnect, we can maintain this momentum and bring together the scale, financing and expertise of all partners to invest in the first mile of food systems. This means translating our shared vision into tangible realities for rural transformation: driving capital into rural areas, generating jobs, and building resilience against future shocks.”
Implementation of AgriConnect has already commenced via the International Development Association-financed Integrated Rurban Development and Climate Resilience Project (IRDCRP), while the IFC is complementing the initiative by expanding access to finance and enhancing competitiveness in key industries like cinnamon and coconut.
articles.summary: The Government of Sri Lanka, in partnership with the World Bank Group and the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), has officially launched the Sri Lanka AgriConnect Joint Implementation Plan to modernize the nation’s agrifood sector, create jobs, and strengthen food security.

articles.title: India High Commissioner, Deputy Minister inaugurate Ceylon Craft Week 2026
articles.text:
High Commissioner of India to Sri Lanka Santosh Jha, alongside Deputy Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Chathuranga Abeysinghe, inaugurated Ceylon Craft Week 2026 at the Havelock City Mall.
Speaking at the inauguration, High Commissioner Jha highlighted how arts, crafts, and culture transcend geographic borders and nurture long-standing bonds of friendship between nations.
The event brings together master artisans from India, Sri Lanka, and Nepal to showcase their creativity and traditional craftsmanship. The public is invited to explore authentic Indian handicrafts, including Ajrakh block-printed saris, traditional leather juttis and footwear, and natural Indian perfumes, on display at the Havelock City Mall from October 29 through November 1, 2026.

articles.title: Murder over stolen chicken: Supreme Court upholds death sentences of 2 men
articles.text:
The Supreme Court has dismissed an appeal filed by two men convicted of murder, upholding the death sentences imposed by the Tangalle High Court.
The two convicted men, Rajapurage Sugath Weeraratne and Rajamunige Nihal Chaminda alias Mahattaya, had been found guilty of murdering Wijeyamunige Gunawardhena.
A three-judge Supreme Court bench comprising Justices Janak De Silva, Menaka Wijesundera and Sampath B. Abayakoon delivered the ruling on October 30.
The case involved a fatal stabbing following a dispute over the alleged theft of a chicken.
According to court proceedings, an argument had taken place earlier in the day after the victim was accused of stealing a chicken belonging to another villager.
Later that evening, the victim was attacked near his home. His father, who witnessed the incident, testified that the first accused stabbed his son while the second accused held him.
The victim sustained 11 stab wounds and died shortly after the attack.
The two accused challenged their convictions, arguing that the prosecution’s main eyewitness had given contradictory evidence and that the trial court had failed to properly evaluate the defence.
However, the Supreme Court found that the father’s testimony was credible and supported by other witness accounts and medical evidence.
Justice Menaka Wijesundera, delivering the judgment, observed that the eyewitness had satisfactorily withstood cross-examination and had not exaggerated his account of the incident.
The court also noted that the medical evidence concerning the victim’s injuries supported the prosecution’s version of events.
The Supreme Court concluded that the defence had failed to create reasonable doubt about the prosecution’s case.
Accordingly, the court dismissed the appeal and affirmed the findings of the Tangalle High Court and the Court of Appeal.
Justices Janak De Silva and Sampath B. Abayakoon agreed with the judgment.
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has dismissed an appeal filed by two men convicted of murder, upholding the death sentences imposed by the Tangalle High Court. Accordingly, the court dismissed the appeal and affirmed the findings of the Tangalle High Court and the Court of Appeal.

articles.title: Father wins two-year battle against private hospital over newborn’s weight reading
articles.text:
A father’s nearly two-year battle against Ninewells Hospital over an allegedly incorrect weight measurement of his newborn baby has ended in victory, with the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) ordering the private hospital to pay compensation.
Speaking to Newswire, attorney Bhanuka Malaviarachchi, who filed a formal complaint against the hospital in June 2024, said the ruling came after a lengthy fight for justice over an incident involving his 10-day-old baby.
“Regarding a complaint I lodged against Ninewells Hospital, the CAA has finally delivered a verdict in my favour and ordered Ninewells Hospital to compensate me in the sum of Rs. 45,900,” Malaviarachchi told Newswire.
Describing the ordeal, he said the hospital had used a malfunctioning weighing scale to measure his newborn baby’s weight, resulting in medical recommendations based on what he believed was an incorrect reading.
“This was a rather sensitive case involving my newborn baby. The hospital weighed my baby using a malfunctioning weighing scale and prescribed certain medical tests and treatments based on the incorrect reading. However, when I had my baby’s weight checked again at Kings Hospital, it became evident that the reading obtained at Ninewells Hospital was incorrect,” he said.
“It was a hard fought battle, but justice has finally been served,” he added.
According to the case records, the infant was initially weighed at Ninewells Hospital, where an electronic scale recorded a weight of 2.48 kg.
The attending paediatrician expressed concern over the reported weight loss and recommended two laboratory investigations, including a serum bilirubin test.
Concerned by the findings, the parents subsequently took their baby to Kings Hospital, where another paediatrician checked the infant’s weight using two separate scales, recording 2.675 kg.
The difference in readings prompted Malaviarachchi to pursue a complaint with the CAA, questioning the accuracy of the weighing equipment and the medical expenses incurred.
During the inquiry, the complainant submitted a recorded telephone conversation in which, according to the case documents, the paediatrician acknowledged that issues with weighing scales had previously occurred at the hospital.
The records also referred to an inspection conducted by the Measurement Units, Standards and Services Department in August 2024, after the hospital said its weighing equipment had been readjusted.
The inspection report noted that an inactive weighing scale remained inside a consultant room used by paediatricians.
The complaint also raised concerns about the hospital’s admission procedures and room cleanliness during the family’s stay.
Malaviarachchi alleged that his pregnant wife had been required to wait for more than two hours on a plastic chair near the admission counter before her Caesarean section in June 2024.
He also complained about inadequate cleaning of the hospital room allocated to the family.
According to the case documents, Ninewells Hospital denied liability but acknowledged potential admission delays and individual oversights in room maintenance. The hospital also indicated that lobby seating was being replaced following feedback.
Following an inquiry under Section 32 of the Consumer Affairs Authority Act No. 9 of 2003, CAA Chairman Hemantha Samarakoon issued an order directing the hospital to compensate the complainant.
The order, dated September 7, 2026, required the hospital to comply within 30 days, with provisions for further legal action in the event of non-compliance.
Malaviarachchi told Newswire that he had since received the compensation and intended to donate the money to a cancer hospital fund or a hospital in a rural area.
Explaining why he decided to pursue the matter and speak publicly about his experience, he said he hoped the outcome would encourage other patients to stand up for their rights.
“I believe this is a good opportunity to raise public awareness. I heard many of my friends had faced similar experiences,” he told Newswire.
articles.summary: A father’s nearly two-year battle against Ninewells Hospital over an allegedly incorrect weight measurement of his newborn baby has ended in victory, with the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) ordering the private hospital to pay compensation. However, when I had my baby’s weight checked again at Kings Hospital, it became evident that the reading obtained at Ninewells Hospital was incorrect,” he said.

articles.title: Ryanair responds to Sangakkara but remains silent on racism and discrimination allegations
articles.text:
Ryanair has responded to former Sri Lanka cricket captain Kumar Sangakkara over an incident at Dublin Airport, claiming he refused to provide required visa documentation during immigration checks. However, the airline’s reported statement does not directly address his allegations of racism, discriminatory treatment and threatening behaviour by its staff.
Sangakkara accused Ryanair gate personnel of mistreating him and his family while boarding a flight from Dublin to Bristol on October 28.
In a statement reported by The Irish Times and other international media outlets, Ryanair said Sangakkara had refused to provide the necessary visa documentation when requested by a gate agent carrying out mandatory immigration checks.
The airline said the required checks were subsequently completed, his eligibility to travel was verified and he travelled on his scheduled flight.
However, the statement did not specifically respond to Sangakkara’s allegations concerning the language used by airline personnel, their alleged threatening conduct or his claim that the treatment was racially discriminatory.
In his initial social media post, Sangakkara described the experience as shocking and unacceptable, criticising the way staff addressed his family, handled procedures and allegedly threatened them.
He subsequently provided further details of the alleged encounter, claiming that airline personnel had told him that people holding passports like his should expect such treatment.
According to Sangakkara, when he challenged the alleged remark, he was warned that arguing with airline staff could result in him being considered a threat to other passengers and denied boarding.
Sangakkara rejected the suggestion that the treatment amounted to equal application of airline procedures, describing the alleged remarks as racist.
While Ryanair’s explanation addresses the documentation checks that it says prompted the incident, it does not clarify whether the alleged remarks about Sangakkara’s passport were made or whether the conduct of its gate staff has been reviewed.
The airline’s statement also does not indicate whether any internal investigation has been initiated into the accusations of discrimination.
Sangakkara’s allegations have attracted widespread attention on social media, with several users sharing their own experiences of alleged discriminatory treatment while travelling internationally.
The allegations against Ryanair staff have not been independently verified, and the airline has not publicly addressed the specific racism allegations in the statements reviewed.
The incident has raised questions about whether the dispute concerned only mandatory travel documentation or also the manner in which passengers were treated during those checks.
articles.summary: Ryanair has responded to former Sri Lanka cricket captain Kumar Sangakkara over an incident at Dublin Airport, claiming he refused to provide required visa documentation during immigration checks. However, the airline’s reported statement does not directly address his allegations of racism, discriminatory treatment and threatening behaviour by its staff.

articles.title: Sri Lanka Navy seizes 1,500 illegal sea cucumbers and apprehends suspect in Kilinochchi
articles.text:
The Sri Lanka Navy arrested one suspect and seized a small boat carrying approximately 1,500 illegally harvested sea cucumbers during an operation in the Valaipadu lagoon in Kilinochchi yesterday (Oct.29).
Personnel from SLNS Buwaneka, operating under the North Central Naval Command, intercepted the dinghy and discovered the illicit catch being transported without valid permits.
The 35-year-old suspect, a resident of Kiranchi, along with the boat and sea cucumbers, was transferred to the Kilinochchi office of the Department of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources for further legal proceedings.

articles.title: India to provide 430 free electric motorbikes worth Rs 265 mn to Sri Lanka Fisheries officers
articles.text:
India has agreed to provide 430 electric motorbikes to fisheries officials in Sri Lanka under a grant assistance programme worth Rs. 265 million.
A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed between Indian High Commissioner to Sri Lanka Santosh Jha and Secretary to the Ministry of Fisheries, Aquatic and Ocean Resources Dr. B.K. Kolita Kamal Jinadasa.
The signing ceremony was held in the presence of Fisheries Minister Ramalingam Chandrasekar.
According to the Indian High Commission in Colombo, the electric motorbikes will be provided at the request of the Sri Lankan government to field officers attached to several institutions, including the Department of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources, the National Aquaculture Development Authority (NAQDA) and the National Aquatic Resources Research and Development Agency (NARA).
The initiative is expected to improve the operational efficiency and mobility of fisheries officials, enabling faster responses and more regular engagement with fishing communities across the country.
The project will also support the environmental sustainability objectives of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake’s Clean Sri Lanka programme.
The Indian High Commission said the initiative forms part of India’s ongoing development cooperation with Sri Lanka, which covers several sectors, including fisheries, housing, health, education, transport, renewable energy and agriculture.
The High Commission said its development assistance programmes extend to all 25 districts of Sri Lanka.
articles.summary: India has agreed to provide 430 electric motorbikes to fisheries officials in Sri Lanka under a grant assistance programme worth Rs. 265 million.

articles.title: Sri Lankan exporters briefed on new EU regulations on coconut products and spices
articles.text:
The Department of Commerce of Sri Lanka (DOC), in collaboration with the Embassy of Sri Lanka in Brussels and the Ceylon Chamber of Commerce (CCC), organized an awareness session on October 21, 2026, to educate local exporters on the upcoming European Union (EU) Regulation on Mineral Oil Aromatic Hydrocarbons (MOAH) set to take effect on January 1, 2027.
Held at the CCC auditorium, the event drew over 100 participants, including exporters, trade chamber representatives, and government officials, to discuss preventive measures required to protect the export of coconut-based products and spices to the EU.
Director General of Commerce Somasena Mahadiulwewa delivered the opening remarks, emphasizing that the EU market accounts for 24% of Sri Lanka’s total merchandise exports and stressing the importance of staying informed on new regulations to prevent market disruptions. CCC Secretary General and CEO Shiran Fernando echoed these sentiments, while Sri Lanka’s Ambassador to Belgium, Chandana Weerasena, joined virtually to reaffirm the Embassy’s commitment to supporting regulatory compliance and maintaining Sri Lanka’s European market share.
The technical session featured presentations by Chris Downes, Policy and Law Lead Expert for the EU-funded AGRINFO programme implemented by COLEAD, and Claus-Michael Brieber, Quality Senior Expert (Food) at Food Safety First.
Experts covered crucial topics including maximum MOAH levels, monitoring MOSH and MOAH, timelines, mitigation strategies and proper sampling methods.
Additionally, Rasika Seneviratne, Vice President of the Sri Lanka Food Processors Association, outlined specific contamination sources and preventive measures for local coconut and spice industries. Charitha Yattogoda, Director of Commerce and Head of the Trade Promotion and Bilateral (West) Division, moderated the session and underscored the urgent need to enhance local laboratory testing and certification capacities to meet international standards.
articles.summary: The Department of Commerce of Sri Lanka (DOC), in collaboration with the Embassy of Sri Lanka in Brussels and the Ceylon Chamber of Commerce (CCC), organized an awareness session on October 21, 2026, to educate local exporters on the upcoming European Union (EU) Regulation on Mineral Oil Aromatic Hydrocarbons (MOAH) set to take effect on January 1, 2027.
