articles.title: Sarath Weerasekara threatens Rs. 100 million legal action against Kingsbury Hotel over leaking CCTV
articles.text:
Former Public Security Minister Rear Admiral Dr. Sarath Weerasekara has issued a letter of demand to The Kingsbury Hotel in Colombo, threatening legal action seeking Rs. 100 million in damages over the alleged release of manipulated CCTV footage showing his visit to the hotel.
The letter, dated October 29, was sent through his lawyers, Perera Seneviratne Associates, alleging that CCTV footage recorded during his visit to the hotel on October 24 had been manipulated and circulated on several social media platforms.
According to the letter, the footage was allegedly altered to create the misleading impression that Weerasekara and a Buddhist monk entered a hotel room together or at approximately the same time.
His lawyers maintain that the impression created by the footage is false.
The letter further alleges that the hotel released the footage or still images in collusion with individuals operating several Facebook pages and YouTube channels, including Dasatha Lanka News, Channel 4, Gune Aiyage Kamare and Cyber News LK.
Weerasekara’s lawyers also allege that one Facebook page published the video with a misleading claim involving his secretary, falsely identifying the individual as former National Intelligence chief Hendawitharana.
The lawyers argue that the original CCTV recordings were under the exclusive possession and control of the hotel and could not have been circulated without its knowledge or involvement.
They also claim that the alleged release of the footage without Weerasekara’s consent violated his privacy and the hotel’s own privacy policy.
According to the letter, Weerasekara has suffered severe online harassment, mental distress and damage to his reputation following the circulation of the footage.
The former minister has demanded that the hotel, within seven days of the letter, identify those responsible for accessing, altering or releasing the footage and disclose the individuals or organisations to whom it was provided.
He has also demanded the removal of the footage from online platforms, a public clarification acknowledging the alleged manipulation, a written apology and an undertaking against further unauthorised disclosures.
The letter warns that failure to comply would result in legal proceedings without further notice, with Weerasekara reserving the right to claim Rs. 100 million in damages for alleged defamation, invasion of privacy, reputational harm and mental distress.
His lawyers have also indicated that complaints could be lodged with the Police, the Online Safety Commission and the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority.
articles.summary: Former Public Security Minister Rear Admiral Dr. Sarath Weerasekara has issued a letter of demand to The Kingsbury Hotel in Colombo, threatening legal action seeking Rs. 100 million in damages over the alleged release of manipulated CCTV footage showing his visit to the hotel.

articles.title: Met Department issues amber alert for Bay of Bengal as low-pressure system intensifies
articles.text:
The Natural Hazards Early Warning Centre of the Department of Meteorology has issued an amber alert warning naval and fishing communities not to venture into deep-sea areas bounded by 10N-15N and 80E-90E in the Bay of Bengal due to expected strong winds and rough seas.
According to the advisory issued at 4:30 p.m. on October 30 a low-pressure area located over the south Andaman Sea is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify into a depression over the southeast Bay of Bengal and adjoining areas of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Andaman Sea by tomorrow (October 31). The system is forecasted to intensify further while moving towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, India, over the subsequent two days.
Wind speeds in the designated advisory sea areas are expected to reach up to 60 kmph at times, leading to rough sea conditions. Naval and fishing communities currently operating in these designated deep-sea areas are strongly advised to move to safe areas and stay updated on further forecasts and weather bulletins issued by the Department of Meteorology.

articles.title: Sri Lanka’s Colombo inflation edges up to 8.3% in October
articles.text:
Sri Lanka’s inflation rate based on the Colombo Consumer Price Index (CCPI) rose to 8.3 percent in October, up from 8.0 percent recorded in September, according to the latest figures released by the Department of Census and Statistics.
The data highlights a broad-based price increase across major categories, with food group inflation increasing to 8.8 percent.
Additionally, non-food group inflation also accelerated to 8.0 percent during the period, reflecting continued upward pressure on essential living expenses.

articles.title: Gen Z and Millennium UNP: New decision from UNP
articles.text:
The United National Party (UNP) has officially introduced two new membership categories targeting younger generations, as part of efforts to restructure its party membership.
The new categories, Millennium UNP and Gen Z UNP, were formally announced at a meeting of the party’s Working Committee held at its Sirikotha headquarters in Pitakotte.
UNP Leader and former President Ranil Wickremesinghe confirmed the representation of both groups during the meeting.
According to the party, Millennium UNP will represent individuals aged between 35 and 40, while Gen Z UNP will represent young people born after 2000.
UNP Chairman Vajira Abeywardena claimed this was the first time a political party in Sri Lanka had introduced membership categories specifically representing two generations.
Abeywardena said the Working Committee also held extensive discussions on the party’s Green Paper, which proposes a 20-year development programme instead of traditional five-year election manifestos.
He further said Wickremesinghe had outlined the need for political parties to work together under a common understanding rather than operating independently.
The former President also explained a proposed mechanism for achieving cooperation among political parties, Abeywardena added.
articles.summary: The United National Party (UNP) has officially introduced two new membership categories targeting younger generations, as part of efforts to restructure its party membership. The new categories, Millennium UNP and Gen Z UNP, were formally announced at a meeting of the party’s Working Committee held at its Sirikotha headquarters in Pitakotte.

articles.title: Hackers steal $6.3 billion from Binance in record heist blamed on North Korea
articles.text:
Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, suspended withdrawals after hackers broke into its digital wallets and stole $6 billion in what appears to be the biggest crypto heist ever.
Binance said late Thursday that its initial investigation indicated the hack went through an engineer’s laptop, “which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.” Blockchain evidence suggests the hack originated in North Korea, according to multiple crypto-tracing firms.
A team of cryptocurrency firms managed to freeze about $3 billion of the stolen loot amid a frenetic battle with the hackers to find and control the digital money.
Binance co-CEO Richard Tend said on X that the attack was not a “one-click” action, but rather a complex process. The investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual nor found evidence of any wallet private key leak.
Binance said it would cover all losses from the company’s funds and an emergency assets fund, adding “user funds are safe.” The crypto exchange said it had temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals to allow security checks to be completed and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover funds.
The crypto exchange expects withdrawal services to resume by Sunday morning.
Crypto-tracing firm TRM Labs attributed the heist to an elite North Korean hacking unit “based on robust on and off-chain intelligence,” pointing out that “several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists.”
Pangolin Intelligence, another blockchain-tracking firm based in Singapore, said it also believed that a North Korean hacking unit was behind the heist.
“Analyzing the on-chain activity related to this hack and correlating with information gathered from previous known incidents” led to the attribution, said an analyst with Pangolin Intelligence, who did not want to be named for privacy reasons.
“I think the cat and mouse game has barely begun yet,” the Pangolin Intelligence analyst told CNN, adding that North Korea was likely poised to tap a network of money laundering organizations to try to cash out the stolen funds.
Chainalysis, another crypto-tracking company, said it was monitoring stolen funds “moving across multiple blockchains,” including bitcoin and ethereum. A Chainalysis spokesperson told CNN the firm had “high confidence” North Korea was behind the hack.
CNN has reached out to North Korea’s mission at the UN for comment. Pyongyang has previously denied hacking allegations.
CNN has requested comment from the FBI, as well as the US Secret Service, which also investigates cybercrime. In past investigations of big crypto hacks, the FBI has had an on-call team of analysts that worked to freeze some of the money.
If North Korea is proven to be the culprit, it would be little surprise to US law enforcement officials and private experts. North Korean hackers were blamed for the previous record-high crypto hack, when they allegedly stole $1.5 billion from Bybit, another major cryptocurrency exchange. In that case, the attackers stole an amount equal to a significant portion of North Korea’s reported annual gross domestic product in a matter of minutes.
North Korea’s formidable hacking teams are a key source of revenue for the nuclear-armed, sanctions-battered regime, according to current and former US and South Korean officials. Pyongyang-linked hackers have stolen billions of dollars from banks and cryptocurrency firms in the last several years, according to reports from the United Nations and private firms.
A 2023 CNN investigation spotlighted how the South Korean intelligence service worked with private crypto-tracking experts to seize about $1 million in cryptocurrency that North Koreans had stolen from a victim.
Unlike platforms for trading stocks, cryptocurrency exchanges tend to hold digital assets on their users’ behalf, which make them more vulnerable to hackers and theft, particularly given a lack of regulatory oversight within the relatively nascent industry.
Binance was co-founded in 2017 by Canadian national Changpeng Zhao, becoming the world’s largest crypto trading platform within a year of its launch.
However, Zhao stepped down in 2023 after pleading guilty to violating anti-money laundering laws in the US. He was sentenced to four months in federal prison, and was pardoned by President Donald Trump in October last year.
Zhao, who no longer manages the platform but remains its largest shareholder, said on X that he expects user funds to be fully covered by the exchange, pushing back against any suggestion to the contrary in a spat on X with Elon Musk.
Prices of bitcoin and ether, the most widely traded cryptocurrencies, plummeted following news of the Binance breach, but regained some losses to trade about 2-3% lower midday Friday in Hong Kong. (CNN)
articles.summary: Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, suspended withdrawals after hackers broke into its digital wallets and stole $6 billion in what appears to be the biggest crypto heist ever. North Korean hackers were blamed for the previous record-high crypto hack, when they allegedly stole $1.5 billion from Bybit, another major cryptocurrency exchange.

articles.title: Minister explains legal action against Laugfs Gas over supply shortage
articles.text:
Minister of Trade Wasantha Samarasinghe says legal action has been initiated against LAUGFS Gas PLC over allegations of misleading consumers and causing inconvenience to the public by failing to maintain adequate gas supplies.
Speaking to the media, Minister Samarasinghe said the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) had filed a case against the company yesterday (29), which is scheduled to be taken up for hearing on November 11.
The Minister alleged that Laugfs Gas had failed to follow proper procurement procedures, resulting in supply disruptions since last month.
He said the company had previously informed the Ministry of Finance that 3,800 metric tonnes of gas would arrive between October 20 and 28. However, the shipment did not arrive as scheduled.
According to the Minister, Laugfs Gas subsequently informed the CAA and the Ministry of Trade yesterday that the shipment would arrive between November 2 and 5.
Minister Samarasinghe accused the company of deliberately misleading the public and said the authorities had consequently been instructed to initiate legal proceedings.
He further revealed that Laugfs Gas had repeatedly requested permission to release its entire stock of 3,900 metric tonnes of gas at the Hambantota Port terminal to the domestic market.
Under its agreement with the Board of Investment (BOI), the company is required to export 80% of its gas while supplying only 20% to the local market.
However, the Minister said the government had issued a letter yesterday allowing the company to distribute 100% of its gas to the domestic market, subject to repayment of the tax concessions granted for the construction of its Hambantota gas terminal.
He maintained that there were therefore no restrictions preventing Laugfs Gas from supplying the domestic market through the Hambantota terminal.
Meanwhile, Minister Samarasinghe assured consumers that Litro Gas supplies had returned to normal, with approximately 1,200 metric tonnes being distributed daily.
He said Litro Gas was distributing 39,000 metric tonnes this month, compared to its usual monthly supply of 32,000 metric tonnes, to compensate for the shortage caused by Laugfs Gas.
The Minister added that Litro Gas had ordered 41,000 metric tonnes for November to ensure adequate supplies.
He pointed out that Laugfs Gas was expected to supply approximately 6,000 metric tonnes monthly, but had failed to meet this requirement.
Minister Samarasinghe also raised concerns over consumers who had paid deposits ranging from Rs. 10,000 to Rs. 15,000 for Laugfs Gas cylinders but were now unable to obtain refills.
He said the company would have to refund the deposits to affected consumers, enabling them to purchase Litro Gas cylinders.
The Minister reiterated that the government had taken measures to address the supply gap through Litro Gas while pursuing legal action against Laugfs Gas over the alleged disruption and inconvenience caused to consumers.
articles.summary: Minister of Trade Wasantha Samarasinghe says legal action has been initiated against LAUGFS Gas PLC over allegations of misleading consumers and causing inconvenience to the public by failing to maintain adequate gas supplies.

articles.title: Sri Lanka’s prisons hold nearly 40,000 inmates despite capacity for 11,000: BASL President
articles.text:
President of the Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL), Rajeev Amarasuriya, has raised serious concerns over prison overcrowding in Sri Lanka, revealing that facilities designed to accommodate approximately 11,000 inmates currently hold nearly 40,000.
He further revealed that nearly 30,000 prisoners are being held on remand, while almost two-thirds of the prison population are detained in connection with drug-related offences.
Amarasuriya made these remarks today (30), addressing the ceremonial sitting held to welcome Justices Lakmali Karunanayake, Nawarathne Marasinghe and Manjula Tilakaratne to the Court of Appeal.
Referring to a recent visit to the New Magazine Prison in Welikada during a legal aid camp organised by the BASL, Amarasuriya described the conditions he witnessed as appalling and, for many prisoners, inhumane and degrading.
He stressed that the situation highlighted the importance of due process, preventing delays in legal proceedings and upholding the presumption of innocence.
Amarasuriya pointed out that every decision to deprive an individual of liberty before trial carries serious consequences, adding that judges, lawyers and the State share responsibility in this regard.
While acknowledging recent efforts by the Minister of Justice and National Integration and the Ministry Secretary to address prison overcrowding, he expressed hope that the initiatives would produce meaningful results.
“Imprisonment may deprive a person of liberty, but it must never deprive them of human dignity,” he said.
Meanwhile, addressing the newly appointed Court of Appeal judges, the BASL President emphasised the importance of judicial independence, courage and the timely delivery of justice.
He noted that the Court of Appeal plays a crucial role in addressing grievances brought by citizens against the State and safeguarding public confidence in the rule of law.
Amarasuriya warned that excessive reliance on procedural technicalities, without addressing the underlying grievances of litigants, could undermine public trust in the justice system.
He further stressed that judges must remain independent, particularly when faced with political pressure, public expectations or unpopular decisions.
The BASL President also highlighted the professional achievements and contributions of the three newly appointed Court of Appeal judges, extending the Bar Association’s support and cooperation as they assumed their new responsibilities.

Meanwhile, addressing the newly appointed Court of Appeal judges, the BASL President emphasised the importance of judicial independence, courage and the timely delivery of justice.

articles.title: Pakistan rights activist Imaan Mazari and husband jailed for 10 years
articles.text:
An antiterrorism court in Pakistan has sentenced prominent human rights lawyers Imaan Mazari and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, ⁠⁠to 10 years in prison on terrorism-related charges.
Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra announced the verdict on Thursday, following their trial inside Adiala prison in the garrison city of Rawalpindi.
The couple were found guilty of putting “the security of [the England and Wales Cricket] team at risk”, the judge wrote, adding that it “clearly shows the intentions and objective of the accused to create a sense of terror”, according to a copy of the court judgement obtained by the AFP news agency.
At the same time, the ruling conceded that the security breach was “a very common nature ordinary type of incident apparently of removal of a barrier”.
The case relates to an October 2024 incident in which the couple removed road barriers in the capital, Islamabad, along a route designated for the touring England cricket team.
The couple were indicted on October 7, accused of obstructing police and inciting public interest, and pleaded not guilty.
In statements seen by the Reuters news agency, the couple denied the charges, while calling themselves “prisoners of conscience”, adding that ⁠⁠they were being targeted for their human rights work.
In their defence document, the couple had earlier said they were “being made an example to further cement the chilling effect against those who stand (or want to stand) against tyranny, oppression and injustice”.
Relatives criticise judicial process
Shireen Mazari, who is Imaan Mazari’s mother and served as Pakistan’s human rights minister under incarcerated former Prime Minister Imran Khan, said it was a “sham trial without any due process”.
Mazari told the Reuters news agency the couple “were not permitted to defend themselves through their own lawyer, and were not provided with key legal ⁠⁠documents”, adding that the defence would file a petition against the verdict in the Supreme Court.
Amnesty International called the convictions “an indictment of Pakistan’s justice system.”
“It was a test of the judiciary’s ability to uphold the principles of justice and the right to fair trial. It has failed that test miserably,” said Amnesty’s Yasmine Ahmend.
“It is clear that these ‘anti-terrorism’ charges are being used to punish Imaan and Hadi for their human rights advocacy,” she added.
Mazari and Chattha have been in custody since January 23, in a separate case over their social media posts.
A lower court sentenced ‌‌them each to 17 years the next day under Pakistan’s Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, which critics have said is designed to quash antigovernment dissent online.
Although the Supreme Court later suspended those sentences, police re-arrested ‌‌the couple the same day in the security breach case.
“Imaan and Hadi’s re-arrest dispels any pretence that the charges against them are anything other than a politically motivated attempt to punish them for their human rights work”, said Babu Ram Pant, Amnesty International’s Deputy Regional Director for South Asia, adding that the case demonstrates once again the authorities’ willingness to weaponise the legal system against critical voices.
Pakistan’s ⁠⁠law minister, Azam Nazeer Tarar, has repeatedly said the country’s judiciary is independent. (Al Jazeera)
articles.summary:
An antiterrorism court in Pakistan has sentenced prominent human rights lawyers Imaan Mazari and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, ⁠⁠to 10 years in prison on terrorism-related charges. Relatives criticise judicial process
Shireen Mazari, who is Imaan Mazari’s mother and served as Pakistan’s human rights minister under incarcerated former Prime Minister Imran Khan, said it was a “sham trial without any due process”.

articles.title: President appoints advisory council to oversee Anuradhapura Sacred City development
articles.text:
A Presidential Advisory Council comprising 32 members has been appointed to oversee decision-making related to development programmes within the Anuradhapura Sacred City, while ensuring the protection of its archaeological, historical, religious and cultural heritage.
According to the President’s Media Division (PMD), the council has been established to facilitate integrated heritage conservation, management, planning and development within the sacred area.
The council will be co-chaired by the Acting Chief Incumbent of the Atamasthana, Most Venerable Eethalawetunuwewe Gnanatilaka Nayaka Thera, and Chief of Presidential Staff Prabhath Chandrakeerthi.
Ven. Eethalawetunuwewe Gnanatilaka Thera also serves as the Chief Incumbent of the Ruwanweli Chaithyarama, Chancellor of Rajarata University, General Secretary of the Mahavihara Sangha Council and Chief Sanghanayake of the North Central Province.
The council includes senior Buddhist monks, government officials, academics, archaeologists, heritage conservation specialists and representatives of several state institutions.
Among its members are Ven. Professor Kallanchiye Rathanasiri, Chief Incumbent of the Abhayagiriya Chaithyarama, Ven. Kahalle Gnaninda, Chief Incumbent of the Thuparama Chaithyarama, and Ven. Kahatagollawe Medhankara, former Deputy Secretary of the Maha Bodhi Society of India.
Representatives from the Department of Archaeology, Central Cultural Fund, Urban Development Authority, National Physical Planning Department and other relevant institutions have also been appointed to the council.
The membership further includes officials from the Anuradhapura Municipal Council, district administration, Police, irrigation, road development, electricity, water supply and tourism sectors, alongside experts in archaeology, architecture, urban planning and heritage conservation.
According to the PMD, the council has been entrusted with establishing an integrated decision-making mechanism to ensure that development activities within the Anuradhapura Sacred City are carried out while safeguarding its archaeological, historical, religious and cultural significance.

According to the President’s Media Division (PMD), the council has been established to facilitate integrated heritage conservation, management, planning and development within the sacred area.

articles.title: Three injured in factory explosion in Padukka
articles.text:
Three employees have sustained minor injuries in an explosion at a bandage factory in the Meepe area of Padukka today (30), police said.
The injured employees have been admitted to the Homagama Base Hospital for treatment.
According to police, the explosion occurred while workers were attempting to cut and modify a diesel tank using gas equipment.
The tank, which had been removed from a fuel filling station and purchased at an auction, was reportedly intended to be used for storing lubricating oil at the factory.
Police said the explosion occurred as the workers attempted to modify the tank without removing the fuel remaining inside it.
Two male employees sustained injuries in the explosion, while a female employee was hospitalised after a roof tile fell onto her head.
The Padukka Police are conducting further investigations into the incident.
articles.summary: Three employees have sustained minor injuries in an explosion at a bandage factory in the Meepe area of Padukka today (30), police said. Police said the explosion occurred as the workers attempted to modify the tank without removing the fuel remaining inside it.

articles.title: Father sentenced to 54 years in prison for raping underage daughter
articles.text:
The Gampaha High Court has sentenced a man to 54 years of rigorous imprisonment after finding him guilty of raping his daughter, who was under the age of 16.
According to Police, the verdict was delivered on Thursday (29), with the accused found guilty on all three charges filed against him.
The High Court imposed 18 years of rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 50,000 for each charge, amounting to a total prison sentence of 54 years and fines of Rs. 150,000.
The court also ordered the convicted father to pay Rs. 200,000 in compensation to the victim.
Failure to pay the fines will result in an additional three years of imprisonment, while failure to pay the compensation will carry a further two-year prison sentence.
Police said the case was investigated by the Bureau for the Prevention and Investigation of Abuse of Children and Women, which arrested the suspect and initiated legal proceedings.
Meanwhile, Police revealed that the victim’s mother’s partner had previously been convicted by the Panadura High Court of raping the same girl and selling her for money.
In a verdict delivered on June 24, 2024, the Panadura High Court sentenced the man to 15 years of rigorous imprisonment on each of the two charges.
He was also fined Rs. 8,000 and ordered to pay the victim Rs. 500,000 in compensation.
The court further imposed additional prison terms in the event of non-payment of the fines and compensation.
The details were disclosed in a statement issued by the Police Media Division on Friday (30).
articles.summary: The Gampaha High Court has sentenced a man to 54 years of rigorous imprisonment after finding him guilty of raping his daughter, who was under the age of 16. The High Court imposed 18 years of rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 50,000 for each charge, amounting to a total prison sentence of 54 years and fines of Rs. 150,000.
